question: Detail the end-to-end process of performing an external black-box web application penetration test against a React-based single-page application (SPA) that uses JWT bearer tokens stored in HTTP-only, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookies, focusing on the technical steps required to escalate privileges from an unauthenticated user to domain administrator, including payload crafting, session management abuse, and Active Directory integration.
answer:
An external black-box assessment of a React SPA with JWT-in-cookie authentication begins with reconnaissance to fingerprint the stack (Nmap –sV –A, Wappalyzer headers, Burp Suite JS analyzer). You then spider the application while manipulating the “Accept” header (Accept: application/json) to uncover hidden REST endpoints. The SPA likely uses an OAuth2/OIDC flow with PKCE; bypassing PKCE by replaying the authorization code (CVE-2019-20859, “Return-jacking”) grants an authorization code that can be exchanged for an opaque JWT containing the “sub” claim—initially your low-privilege user.

Next, token-side attacks are executed. You extract and modify the JWT using jwt_tool –X a to change the “sub” to “admin”, re-sign with HS256 using the leaked client secret (discovered via /.well-known/openid-configuration → jwks_uri → object transversing in Burp Repeater), then set the cookie via a forged login redirect crafted with csrf-poc.py. The forged JWT is smuggled into a legitimate login flow via “/login?code=STOLEN_CODE&state=XSS_VECTOR” to evade SameSite checks.

Once inside with an admin JWT, the SPA’s GraphQL endpoint (/{tenant}/graphql) likely exposes a “setPassword” mutation. You craft a GraphQL mutation with a 200-character Unicode password; the backend stores it in Active Directory via LDAPS using a vulnerable ntdsutil replication channel (CVE-2021-42278 SamAccountName spoofing). Exploiting this, you create a machine account with a forged SPN, request a Kerberos TGT via Impacket addcomputer.py –computer-name ’WKSTN001$’ –dc-ip <DC_IP>, then perform a Resource-Based Constrained Delegation attack (CVE-2021-42278 + CVE-2021-42287) targeting the Exchange server, ultimately achieving DCSync rights with secretsdump.py SYSTEM=WKSTN001$ hash local NT hash on the DC.

Mitigation: enforce RS256 with rotated JWKS, disable HS256, enable JWT proof-of-possession (PoP) binding to TLS session keys (RFC 7800), patch CVE-2021-42278 hotfix kb5008380, disable LDAP signing downgrade, and block RBCD in GPO. Real-world: APT29’s 2023 campaign abused JWTookie misconfigurations to pivot from external CMS to domain admin using this exact technique.
